review.text: Chicken tikka was tasty but the portion felt smaller than last time. Service was friendly enough.

fields.name: Ember & Spice Grill
fields.tone_notes: Warm, friendly and family-run. We talk to customers like regulars, even on their first visit. Short, upbeat sentences with a little East London charm. Use the customer's first name. Never pushy or salesy. Always say thank you. On bad reviews: apologise sincerely, never argue, and invite them back to make it right.
fields.halal_statement: All our meat is halal, certified by HMC.
fields.allergen_statement: Our kitchen handles nuts, sesame, gluten and dairy. Please tell our team about any allergy before you order.
recovery_offers: A free dessert on your next visit

checks.reason: Warm, uses first name, apologises, says thank you and invites contact to make it right, as the profile's tone notes ask for bad reviews.
Refers to Kofi's Chicken Tikka, the smaller portion and the friendly service.
English reply to an English review, plain and clear.
Opening 'Hi Kofi, thanks for the honest feedback' and closing 'hits the mark' differ from the three previous replies provided. Only 3 of the last 10 were supplied.
No em-dashes, no emojis, no hashtags, and no banned word ('cheap').
Every claim traces to the review or profile: Chicken Tikka, friendly service, smaller portion, phone and email contacts, sign-off.
The only number is the phone number, which matches profile:phone exactly.
'Kofi' matches the reviewer 'Kofi A.' and 'Chicken Tikka' matches the menu.
No food, halal or allergen claims.
No targeting or wording based on personal traits.
Nothing offered in exchange for a review or for changing one.
Only details from the public review are used. The phone and email are the business's own.
No financial, legal, tax or staffing advice.
Phone numbers are allowed in Google review replies.

None of the maker's rules are broken: English reply, no argument, no refund or compensation offered, no staff named, correct sign-off. The review is a 3-star complaint about portion size, which is not an escalation case.
